editorial:
Imagine stepping back into 1976 when ABBA was taking over the entire world. You get to hang out with Agnetha, Björn, Benny, and Frida right as they are working on their hit album Arrival. The vibe is super relaxed and intimate, giving you a peek behind the curtain of their massive fame. Instead of a polished corporate film, it feels like a home movie where you see the band members chatting in Swedish and just being themselves. You will see them in the studio at a secret location, which makes the whole experience feel like you are in on a big secret.

What really makes this special is the rare archive footage and the personal photos from their own collections. The pacing is steady, though some of the interviews might feel slow if you just want the hits. However, seeing Stig play the acoustic guitar is a fun little bonus. If you are a music fan, you should definitely check this out. You can hunt for a digital copy to stream in 4K Ultra HD on Prime Video or maybe rent it on Apple TV for a quick movie night. For the true super-fans, adding the physical Blu-ray to your collection is the way to go.
endingExplained: The film wraps up by showing the finished results of their hard work in the studio. You see the group performing their big hits on stage, proving that all those secret recording sessions actually paid off. It ends with a feeling of triumph as they cement their place as global superstars. There is no big plot twist since it is a documentary, but it closes with a heartwarming look at their friendship and musical chemistry.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves disco music and pop history.
